1.1:
I cried to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 when I was in distress,
To Elohim when sinners assailed.
1.2:
Suddenly the alarm of war was heard before me;
I said, He will listen to me, for I am full of righteousness.
1.3:
I thought in my heart that I was full of righteousness,
Because I was well off and had become rich in children.
1.4:
Their wealth spread to the whole earth,
And their esteem to the end of the earth.
1.5:
They were exalted to the stars;
They said they would never fall.
1.6:
But they became insolent in their prosperity,
And they were without understanding,
1.7:
Their sins were in secret,
And even I had no knowledge of them.
1.8:
Their transgressions went beyond those of the nations before them;
They utterly polluted the qodesh things of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

10.1:
Ashrĕ is the man whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 remembers with reproving,
And whom He restrains from the way of evil with strokes,
That he may be cleansed from sin, that it may not be multiplied.
10.2:
He who makes ready his back for strokes shall be cleansed,
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is good to those who endure discipline.
10.3:
For He makes straight the ways of the righteous,
And does not pervert them by His discipline.
10.4:
And the mercy of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is upon those who love Him in truth,
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 remembers His servants in mercy.
10.5:
For the testimony is in the Torah of the eternal covenant,
The testimony of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is on the ways of men in His visitation.
10.6:
Just and kind is our Aḏon in His judgments forever,
And Yisra’ĕl shall praise the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in gladness.
10.7:
And the pious shall give thanks in the assembly of the people;
And on the poor shall Elohim have mercy in the gladness of Yisra’ĕl;
10.8:
For good and merciful is Elohim forever,
And the assemblies of Yisra’ĕl shall esteem the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
The deliverance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be upon the house of Yisra’ĕl to everlasting gladness!

11.1: Blow the trumpet in Tsiyon to summon the qodeshim,
11.2:
Let the voice of him who brings good news be heard in Yerushalayim;
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has had pity on Yisra’ĕl in visiting them.
11.3:
Stand on the height, O Yerushalayim, and see your children,
From the East and the West, gathered together by the Aḏon;
11.4:
From the North they come in the gladness of their Elohim,
From the isles far away Elohim has gathered them.
11.5: High mountains He has abased into a plain for them;
11.6:
The hills fled at their entrance.
The woods gave them shelter as they passed by;
11.7:
Every sweet-smelling tree Elohim caused to spring up for them,
That Yisra’ĕl might pass by in the visitation of the esteem of their Elohim.

12.1:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, deliver my being from the lawless and wicked man,
From the tongue that is lawless and slanderous, and speaks lies and deceit.
12.2:
Manifoldly twisted are the words of the tongue of the wicked man,
Even as among a people a fire that burns up their beauty.
12.3:
So he delights to fill houses with a lying tongue,
To cut down the trees of gladness which sets on fire transgressors,
12.5: In flaming fire may the slanderous tongue perish far away from the pious!
12.6:
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 preserve the quiet being that hates the unrighteous;
And may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 establish the man who follows peace at home.

13.1:
The right hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has covered me;
The right hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spared us.
13.2:
The arm of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has saved us from the sword that passed through,
From famine and the death of sinners.
13.3:
Harmful beasts ran upon them:
With their teeth they tore their flesh,
And with their molars crushed their bones.
But from all these things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 delivered us.
13.4:
The righteous was troubled on account of his errors,
Lest he should be taken away along with the sinners;
13.5:
For terrible is the overthrow of the sinner;
But not one of all these things touches the righteous.
For not alike are the discipline of the righteous for sins done in ignorance,
And the overthrow of the sinners.
13.7:
Secretly is the righteous disciplined,
Lest the sinner rejoice over the righteous.
13.8:
For He corrects the righteous as a beloved son,
And his chastisement is as that of a first-born.
13.10:
But sinners shall be taken away into destruction,
And their memorial shall be found no more.
13.11:
But upon the pious is the mercy of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
And upon those who fear Him His mercy.

14.1:
Faithful is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to those who love Him in truth,
To those who endure His discipline,
To those who walk in the righteousness of His commandments,
In the Torah which He commanded us that we might live.
14.2:
The pious of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall live by it forever;
The Paradise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the trees of life, are His pious ones.
14.5:
And they do not remember Elohim.
For the ways of men are known before Him at all times,
And He knows the secrets of the heart before they come to pass.
14.6:
Therefore their inheritance is She’ol and darkness and destruction,
And they shall not be found in the day when the righteous obtain mercy;
14.7: But the pious of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall inherit life in gladness.

15.1:
When I was in distress I called upon the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
I hoped for the help of the Elohim of Ya’aqoḇ and was saved;
15.2: For the hope and refuge of the poor are You, O Elohim.
15.3: For who, O Elohim, is strong except to give thanks to You in truth?
15.4: And in what is a man powerful except in giving thanks to Your name?
15.5:
A new psalm with song in gladness of heart,
The fruit of the lips with the well-tuned instrument of the tongue,
The first-fruits of the lips from a pious and righteous heart—
15.6:
He who offers these things shall never be shaken by evil;
The flame of fire and the wrath against the unrighteous shall not touch him,
15.7:
When it goes forth from the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 against sinners,
To destroy all the substance of sinners,
15.8:
For the mark of Elohim is upon the righteous that they may be saved.
Famine and sword and pestilence shall be far from the righteous,
15.10: For the mark of destruction is upon their forehead.
15.11:
And the inheritance of sinners is destruction and darkness,
And their iniquities shall pursue them to She’ol beneath.
15.12: Their inheritance shall not be found by their children,
15.13:
For sins shall lay waste the houses of sinners.
And sinners shall perish forever in the day of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s judgment,
15.14: When Elohim visits the earth with His judgment.

16.1:
When my being slumbered, being far from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I had all but slipped down to the pit,
When I was far from Elohim, my being had been nearly poured out to death,
I had been near to the gates of She’ol with the sinner, when my being departed from the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of Yisra’ĕl—
Had 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 not helped me with His everlasting mercy.
16.4:
He pricked me, as a horse is pricked, that I might serve Him,
My Savior and helper at all times saved me.
16.5:
I will give thanks to You, O Elohim, for You have helped me to my deliverance;
And have not counted me with sinners to my destruction.
16.6:
Do not remove Your mercy from me, O Elohim,
Nor Your memorial from my heart until I die.
16.7:
Rule me, O Elohim, keeping me back from wicked sin,
And from every wicked woman who causes the simple to stumble.
16.8:
And do not let the beauty of a lawless woman beguile me,
Nor anyone who is subject to unprofitable sin.
16.9:
Establish the works of my hands before You,
And preserve my goings in the remembrance of You.
16.10:
Protect my tongue and my lips with words of truth;
Anger and unreasoning wrath put far from me.
16.11:
Murmuring, and impatience in affliction, remove far from me,
When, if I sin, You discipline me that I may return to You.
16.12:
But with goodwill and cheerfulness support my being;
When You strengthen my being, what is given to me will be sufficient for me.
16.13:
For if You do not give strength,
Who can endure chastisement with poverty?
16.14:
When a man is rebuked by means of his corruption,
Your testing of him is in his flesh and in the affliction of poverty.
16.15: If the righteous endures in all these trials, he shall receive mercy from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

17.1:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You are our Meleḵ forever and ever,
For in You, O Elohim, our being boasts.
17.2:
How long are the days of man’s life upon the earth?
As are his days, so is the hope set upon him.
17.3:
But we hope in Elohim, our deliverer;
For the might of our Elohim is forever with mercy,
17.4: And the reign of our Elohim is forever over the nations in judgment.
17.5:
You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, chose Dawiḏ to be meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl,
And swore to him concerning his seed that his reign should never fail before You.
17.7:
They in no way esteemed Your honorable name;
They set a worldly monarchy in place of that which was their excellency;
17.8:
They laid waste the throne of Dawiḏ in tumultuous arrogance.
But You, O Elohim, cast them down and removed their seed from the earth,
17.9: In that there rose up against them a man who was alien to our race.
17.10:
According to their sins You recompensed them, O Elohim;
So that it befell them according to their deeds.
17.11:
Elohim showed them no pity;
He sought out their seed and did not let one of them go free.
17.12: Faithful is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in all His judgments which He does upon the earth.
17.13:
The lawless one laid waste our land so that none inhabited it,
They destroyed young and old and their children together.
17.14:
In the heat of His anger He sent them away even to the west,
And He exposed the rulers of the land unsparingly to derision.
17.15:
Being an alien the enemy acted proudly,
And his heart was alien from our Elohim.
17.16:
And all things, whatever he did in Yerushalayim,
As also the nations in the cities of their strength.
17.17:
And the children of the covenant in the midst of the mingled peoples surpassed them.
There was not among them one who worked mercy and truth in the midst of Yerushalayim.
17.18:
Those who loved the assemblies of the pious fled from them,
As sparrows that fly from their nest.
17.19:
They wandered in deserts that their lives might be saved from harm,
And precious in the eyes of those who lived abroad was any who escaped alive from them.
17.20: Over the whole earth were they scattered by lawless men.
17.22: The meleḵ was a transgressor, and the judge disobedient, and the people sinful.
17.23:
See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and raise up to them their meleḵ, the son of Dawiḏ,
At the time in which You see, O Elohim, that he may reign over Yisra’ĕl Your servant,
17.24: And gird him with strength, that he may shatter unrighteous rulers,
17.25:
And that he may purge Yerushalayim from nations that trample her down to destruction.
Wisely, righteously he shall thrust out sinners from the inheritance,
He shall destroy the pride of the sinner as a potter’s vessel.
With a rod of iron he shall break in pieces all their substance,
17.28:
And he shall gather together a qodesh people, whom he shall lead in righteousness,
And he shall judge the tribes of the people that has been made qadosh by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim.
17.29:
And he shall not allow unrighteousness to lodge any more in their midst,
Nor shall there dwell with them any man who knows wickedness,
17.30:
For he shall know them, that they are all sons of their Elohim.
And he shall divide them according to their tribes upon the land,
17.31:
And neither sojourner nor alien shall sojourn with them any more.
He shall judge peoples and nations in the wisdom of his righteousness. Selah.
17.32:
And he shall have the nations to serve him under his yoke;
And he shall esteem 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in a place to be seen by all the earth;
17.33: And he shall purge Yerushalayim, making it qodesh as of old:
17.34:
So that nations shall come from the ends of the earth to see his esteem,
Bringing as gifts her sons who had fainted,
17.35:
And to see the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, with which Elohim has esteemed her.
And he shall be a righteous meleḵ, taught by Elohim, over them,
17.36:
And there shall be no unrighteousness in his days in their midst,
For all shall be qodesh and their meleḵ the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.37:
For he shall not put his trust in horse and rider and bow,
Nor shall he multiply for himself gold and silver for war,
Nor shall he gather confidence from a multitude for the day of battle.
17.38:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself is his Meleḵ, the hope of him who is mighty through his hope in Elohim.
All nations shall be in fear before him,
17.39: For he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth forever.
17.40: He will baraḵ the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with wisdom and gladness,
17.41:
And he himself will be pure from sin, so that he may rule a great people.
He will rebuke rulers, and remove sinners by the might of his word;
17.43: And the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will be with him: he will be strong and will not stumble;
17.44:
His hope will be in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: who then can prevail against him?
He will be mighty in his works, and strong in the fear of Elohim,
17.45:
He will be shepherding the flock of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 faithfully and righteously,
And will let none among them stumble in their pasture.
17.46:
He will lead them all rightly,
And there will be no pride among them that any among them should be oppressed.
17.47:
This will be the majesty of the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl whom Elohim knows;
He will raise him up over the house of Yisra’ĕl to correct him.
17.48:
His words shall be more refined than costly gold, the choicest;
In the assemblies he will judge the peoples, the tribes of the qodeshim.
17.49: His words shall be like the words of the qodeshim in the midst of qodesh peoples.
17.50:
Ashrĕ are those who shall be in those days,
In that they shall see the good fortune of Yisra’ĕl which Elohim shall bring to pass in the gathering together of the tribes.
17.51:
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hasten His mercy upon Yisra’ĕl!
May He deliver us from the uncleanness of profane enemies!
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself is our Meleḵ forever and ever.

18.1:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Your mercy is over the works of Your hands forever;
Your goodness is over Yisra’ĕl with a rich gift.
18.2: Your eyes look upon them, so that none of them suffers want;
18.3:
Your ears listen to the hopeful prayer of the poor.
Your judgments are executed upon the whole earth in mercy;
18.4:
And Your love is toward the seed of Aḇraham, the children of Yisra’ĕl.
Your chastisement is upon us as upon a first-born, only-begotten son,
18.5: To turn back the obedient being from folly that is done in ignorance.
18.6:
May Elohim cleanse Yisra’ĕl for the day of mercy and beraḵah,
For the day of choice when He brings back His anointed.
18.7:
Ashrĕ shall they be who shall be in those days,
In that they shall see the goodness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He shall perform for the generation that is to come,
18.8:
Under the rod of discipline of the Meleḵ’s anointed in the fear of his Elohim,
In the spirit of wisdom and righteousness and strength;
18.9:
That he may direct every man in the works of righteousness by the fear of Elohim,
That he may establish them all before the Aḏon,
18.10: A good generation living in the fear of Elohim in the days of mercy. Selah.
18.11: Great is our Elohim and esteemed, dwelling in the highest.
18.12:
It is He who has established in their courses the lights of the shamayim for determining seasons from year to year,
And they have not turned aside from the way which He appointed them.
18.13:
In the fear of Elohim they pursue their path every day,
From the day Elohim created them and forever.
18.14:
And they have not erred since the day He created them.
Since the generations of old they have not withdrawn from their path,
Unless Elohim commanded them to do so by the command of His servants.

2.1:
When the sinner grew proud, with a battering-ram he cast down fortified walls,
And You did not restrain him.
2.2:
Alien nations ascended Your altar,
They trampled it proudly with their sandals;
2.3:
Because the sons of Yerushalayim had defiled the qodesh things of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
Had profaned with iniquities the offerings of Elohim.
2.4: Therefore He said: Cast them far from Me;
2.5:
It was despised before Elohim,
It was utterly dishonored;
2.6:
The sons and the daughters were in grievous captivity,
Sealed was their neck, branded was it among the nations.
2.7:
According to their sins He has done to them,
For He has left them in the hands of those who prevailed.
2.8:
He has turned away His face from pitying them,
Young and old and their children together;
2.9: For they had done evil one and all, in not listening.
2.10:
And the shamayim were angry,
And the earth abhorred them;
2.11: For no man upon it had done what they did,
2.12: And the earth recognized all Your righteous judgments, O Elohim.
2.13:
They set the sons of Yerushalayim to be mocked in return for the whores in her;
Every traveler went in, in the full light of day.
2.15:
Because they had defiled themselves with unnatural intercourse.
I am pained in my bowels and my inward parts for these things.
2.16:
And yet I will justify You, O Elohim, in uprightness of heart,
For in Your judgments is Your righteousness displayed, O Elohim.
2.17:
For You have rendered to the sinners according to their deeds,
Indeed, according to their sins, which were very wicked.
2.18: You have uncovered their sins, that Your judgment might be manifest;
2.19:
You have wiped out their memorial from the earth.
Elohim is a righteous judge,
And He shows no partiality.
2.20:
For the nations reproached Yerushalayim, trampling it down;
Her beauty was dragged down from the throne of esteem.
2.21:
She girded on sackcloth instead of fine clothing,
A rope was about her head instead of a crown.
2.22: She put off the esteemed diadem which Elohim had set upon her,
2.23: In dishonor was her beauty cast upon the ground.
2.24:
And I saw and entreated 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and said,
Long enough, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, has Your hand been heavy on Yisra’ĕl, in bringing the nations upon them.
2.25: For they have made sport unsparingly in wrath and fierce anger;
2.26: And they will make an utter end, unless You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, rebuke them in Your wrath.
2.27: For they have done it not in zeal, but in lust of being,
2.28: Pouring out their wrath upon us with a view to plunder.
2.29:
Do not delay, O Elohim, to recompense them on their heads,
To turn the pride of the dragon into dishonor.
2.31:
His body, too, borne here and there on the billows with much insolence,
With none to bury him, because He had rejected him with dishonor.
He did not reflect that he was a man.
2.32: And did not reflect on the latter end;
2.34:
He is Meleḵ over the shamayim,
And judges melaḵim and reigns.
2.35:
It is He who sets me up in esteem,
And brings down the proud to eternal destruction in dishonor,
Because they did not know Him.
2.36:
And now see, you princes of the earth,
the judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
For a great Meleḵ and righteous is He,
judging all that is under the shamayim.
2.37:
Baraḵ Elohim, you who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with wisdom,
For the mercy of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will be upon those who fear Him, in the Judgment;
2.38:
So that He will distinguish between the righteous and the sinner,
And recompense the sinners forever according to their deeds;
2.39:
And have mercy on the righteous, delivering him from the affliction of the sinner,
And recompensing the sinner for what he has done to the righteous.
2.40:
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is good to those who call upon Him in patience,
Doing according to His mercy to His pious ones,
Establishing them at all times before Him in strength.
2.41: Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 forever before His servants.

3.1:
Why do you sleep, O my being,
And not baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
3.2:
Sing a new song,
To Elohim who is worthy to be praised.
Sing and be watchful for His awakening,
For good is a psalm sung to Elohim from a glad heart.
3.3:
The righteous remember 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at all times,
With thanksgiving and declaration of the righteousness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s judgments.
3.4:
The righteous does not despise the discipline of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
His will is always before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.5:
The righteous stumbles and holds 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 righteous:
He falls and looks out for what Elohim will do to him;
3.6: He seeks out from where his deliverance will come.
3.7:
The steadfastness of the righteous is from Elohim their deliverer;
Sin upon sin does not lodge in the house of the righteous.
3.8:
The righteous continually searches his house,
To remove utterly all iniquity done by him in error.
3.9: He makes atonement for sins of ignorance by fasting and afflicting his being,
3.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 counts guiltless every pious man and his house.
3.11:
The sinner stumbles and curses his life,
The day when he was begotten, and his mother’s birth pains.
3.12: He adds sins to sins, while he lives;
3.13:
He falls—truly grievous is his fall—and rises no more.
The destruction of the sinner is forever,
3.14:
And he shall not be remembered, when the righteous is visited.
This is the portion of sinners forever.
3.16:
But those who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall rise to life eternal,
And their life shall be in the light of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and shall come to an end no more.

4.1:
Why do you sit, O profane man, in the council of the pious,
Seeing that your heart is far removed from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
Provoking with transgressions the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl?
4.2:
Extravagant in speech, extravagant in outward appearance beyond all men,
Is he who is severe of speech in condemning sinners in judgment.
4.3:
And his hand is first upon him as though he acted in zeal,
And yet he is himself guilty of manifold sins and of wantonness.
4.4:
His eyes are upon every woman without distinction;
His tongue lies when he makes a contract with an oath.
4.5:
By night and in secret he sins as though unseen,
With his eyes he talks to every woman of evil compacts.
4.6: He is swift to enter every house with cheerfulness as though guileless.
4.7:
Let Elohim remove those who live in hypocrisy in the company of the pious,
Even the life of such a one with corruption of his flesh and penury.
4.8:
Let Elohim reveal the deeds of the men-pleasers,
The deeds of such a one with laughter and derision;
4.9:
That the pious may count righteous the judgment of their Elohim,
When sinners are removed from before the righteous,
4.10: Even the man-pleaser who utters law deceitfully.
4.11:
And their eyes are fixed upon any man’s house that is still secure,
That they may, like the Serpent, destroy the wisdom of … with words of transgressors,
4.12: His words are deceitful that he may accomplish his wicked desire.
4.13:
He never ceases from scattering families as though they were orphans,
Indeed, he lays waste a house on account of his lawless desire.
4.14: He deceives with words, saying, There is none who sees, or judges.
4.15:
He fills one house with lawlessness,
And then his eyes are fixed upon the next house,
To destroy it with words that give wing to desire.
Yet with all these his being, like She’ol, is not satisfied.
4.16:
Let his portion, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, be dishonored before You;
Let him go forth groaning and come home cursed.
4.17:
Let his life be spent in anguish, and penury, and want, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
Let his sleep be beset with pains and his waking with perplexities.
4.18:
Let sleep be withdrawn from his eyelids at night;
Let him fail dishonorably in every work of his hands.
4.19:
Let him come home empty-handed to his house,
And his house be void of everything with which he could satisfy his appetite.
4.20: Let his old age be spent in childless loneliness until his removal by death.
4.21:
Let the flesh of the men-pleasers be torn by wild beasts,
And let the bones of the lawless lie dishonored in the sight of the sun.
4.22: Let ravens peck out the eyes of the hypocrites.
4.23:
For they have laid waste many houses of men, in dishonor,
And scattered them in their lust;
4.24:
And they have not remembered Elohim,
Nor feared Elohim in all these things;
4.25:
But they have provoked Elohim’s anger and vexed Him.
May He remove them from the earth,
Because with deceit they beguiled the beings of the flawless.
4.26: Ashrĕ are those who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in their flawlessness;
4.27:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall deliver them from deceitful men and sinners,
And deliver us from every stumbling-block of the lawless men.
4.28:
Let Elohim destroy those who insolently work all unrighteousness,
For a great and mighty judge is the Meleḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in righteousness.
4.29: Let Your mercy, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, be upon all those who love You.

5.1:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, I will praise Your name with joy,
In the midst of those who know Your righteous judgments.
5.2: For You are good and merciful, the refuge of the poor;
5.3: When I cry to You, do not silently disregard me.
5.4: For no man takes spoil from a mighty man;
5.5: Who, then, can take anything of all that You have made, unless You Yourself give?
5.6:
For man and his portion lie before You in the balance;
He cannot add to, so as to enlarge, what has been prescribed by You.
O Elohim, when we are in distress we call upon You for help,
And You do not turn back our petition, for You are our Elohim.
5.8:
Do not cause Your hand to be heavy upon us,
Lest through necessity we sin.
5.9:
Even though You do not restore us, we will not keep away;
But to You we will come.
5.10:
For if I hunger, to You I will cry, O Elohim;
And You will give to me.
5.12: And if they hunger, to You they lift up their face.
5.13:
Melaḵim and rulers and peoples You nourish, O Elohim;
And who is the help of the poor and needy, if not You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
5.14:
And You will listen—for who is good and gentle but You—
Making glad the being of the humble by opening Your hand in mercy.
5.15:
Man’s goodness is bestowed grudgingly and …;
And if he repeats it without murmuring, even that is marvelous.
5.16:
But Your gift is great in goodness and wealth,
And he whose hope is set on You shall have no lack of gifts.
5.17: Upon the whole earth is Your mercy, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in goodness.
5.18: Ashrĕ is he whom Elohim remembers in granting to him a due sufficiency;
5.19: If a man abounds too much, he sins.
5.20:
Sufficient are moderate means with righteousness,
And by this the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 becomes abundance with righteousness.
5.21:
Those who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rejoice in good gifts,
And Your goodness is upon Yisra’ĕl in Your reign.
Beruḵah is the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for He is our Meleḵ.

6.1: Ashrĕ is the man whose heart is fixed to call upon the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
6.2: When he remembers the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, he will be saved.
6.3:
His ways are made even by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
And the works of his hands are preserved by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim.
6.4: At what he sees in his bad dreams, his being shall not be troubled;
6.5: When he passes through rivers and the tossing of the seas, he shall not be dismayed.
6.6: He rises from his sleep, and baraḵ the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄:
6.7:
When his heart is at peace, he sings to the name of his Elohim,
And he entreats 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for all his house.
6.8:
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hears the prayer of everyone who fears Elohim,
And every request of the being that hopes for Him 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 accomplishes.
6.9: Baruḵ is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who shows mercy to those who love Him in sincerity.

7.1:
Do not make Your dwelling far from us, O Elohim;
Lest those who hate us without cause assail us.
7.2:
For You have rejected them, O Elohim;
Do not let their foot trample upon Your qodesh inheritance.
7.3:
Discipline us Yourself in Your good pleasure;
But do not give us up to the nations;
7.4:
For, if You send pestilence,
You Yourself give it charge concerning us;
For You are merciful,
And will not be angry to the point of consuming us.
7.5: While Your name dwells in our midst, we shall find mercy;
7.6:
And the nations shall not prevail against us.
For You are our shield,
7.7: And when we call upon You, You listen to us;
7.8:
For You will pity the seed of Yisra’ĕl forever
And You will not reject them:
But we shall be under Your yoke forever,
And under the rod of Your discipline.
7.9:
You will establish us in the time that You help us,
Showing mercy to the house of Ya’aqoḇ on the day on which You promised to help them.

8.1:
Distress and the sound of war has my ear heard;
The sound of a trumpet announcing slaughter and calamity,
8.2:
The sound of many people as of an exceedingly high wind,
As a tempest with mighty fire sweeping through the Negeḇ.
8.3: And I said in my heart; Surely Elohim judges us;
8.4: A sound I hear moving toward Yerushalayim, the qodesh city.
8.5: My loins were broken at what I heard, my knees tottered:
8.6: My heart was afraid, my bones were dismayed like flax.
8.8:
Elohim laid bare their sins in the full light of day;
All the earth came to know the righteous judgments of Elohim.
8.9: In secret places underground their iniquities were committed to provoke Him to anger;
8.10: They caused confusion, son with mother and father with daughter;
8.11:
They committed adultery, every man with his neighbor’s wife.
They concluded covenants with one another with an oath concerning these things;
8.12: They plundered the qodesh place of Elohim, as though there was no avenger.
8.13:
They trod the altar of the Meleḵ, coming straight from all manner of uncleanness;
And with menstrual blood they defiled the sacrifices, as though these were common flesh.
8.14: They left no sin undone in which they did not surpass the nations.
8.15:
Therefore Elohim mingled for them a spirit of wandering;
And gave them to drink a cup of undiluted wine, that they might become drunk.
8.16: He brought him who is from the end of the earth, who strikes mightily;
8.17: He decreed war against Yerushalayim, and against her land.
8.18:
The princes of the land went to meet him with joy: they said to him:
Welcome is your coming! Come, enter in peace.
8.19:
They made the rough ways even, before his entry;
They opened the gates to Yerushalayim, they crowned its walls.
8.20:
As a father enters the house of his sons, so he entered Yerushalayim in peace;
He established his feet there in great safety.
8.21: He captured her fortresses and the wall of Yerushalayim;
8.22: For Elohim Himself led him in safety, while they wandered.
8.23:
He destroyed their princes and everyone wise in counsel;
He poured out the blood of the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, like the water of uncleanness.
8.24: He led away their sons and daughters, whom they had begotten in defilement.
8.25: They did according to their uncleanness, even as their fathers had done:
8.26: They defiled Yerushalayim and the things that had been made qadosh to the name of Elohim.
8.27: But Elohim has shown Himself righteous in His judgments upon the nations of the earth;
8.28: And the pious servants of Elohim are like innocent lambs in their midst.
8.29: Worthy to be praised is the Aḏon who judges the whole earth in His righteousness.
8.30: See now, O Elohim, You have shown us Your judgment in Your righteousness;
8.31:
Our eyes have seen Your judgments, O Elohim.
We have justified Your name that is honored forever;
8.32: For You are the Elohim of righteousness, judging Yisra’ĕl with discipline.
8.33: Turn, O Elohim, Your mercy upon us, and have pity upon us;
8.34: Gather together the dispersed of Yisra’ĕl, with mercy and goodness;
8.35:
For Your faithfulness is with us.
And though we have stiffened our neck, yet You are the One who disciplines us;
8.36: Do not overlook us, O our Elohim, lest the nations swallow us up, as though there were none to deliver.
8.37:
But You are our Elohim from the beginning,
And upon You is our hope set, O Aḏonai;
8.38:
And we will not depart from You,
For good are Your judgments upon us.
8.39:
Ours and our children’s be Your good pleasure forever;
O Aḏonai our Savior, we shall never again be moved.
8.40:
The Aḏon is worthy to be praised for His judgments with the mouth of His pious ones;
And baruḵ be Yisra’ĕl of the Aḏon forever.

9.1:
When Yisra’ĕl was led away captive into a strange land,
When they fell away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who redeemed them,
9.2:
They were cast away from the inheritance, which the Meleḵ had given them.
Among every nation were the dispersed of Yisra’ĕl according to the word of Elohim,
9.3: That You might be justified, O Elohim, in Your righteousness by reason of our transgressions:
9.4: For You are a just judge over all the peoples of the earth.
9.5: For from Your knowledge none who does unjustly is hidden,
9.6:
And the righteous deeds of Your pious ones are before You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
Where, then, can a man hide himself from Your knowledge, O Elohim?
9.7:
Our works are subject to our own choice and power
To do right or wrong in the works of our hands;
9.8: And in Your righteousness You visit the sons of men.
9.9:
He who does righteousness lays up life for himself with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
And he who does wrongly forfeits his life to destruction;
9.10:
For the judgments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are given in righteousness to every man and his house.
To whom are You good, O Elohim, except to those who call upon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
9.12: He cleanses from sins a being when it makes confession, when it makes acknowledgment;
9.13: For shame is upon us and upon our faces on account of all these things.
9.14: And to whom does He forgive sins, except to those who have sinned?
9.15:
You baraḵ the righteous, and do not reprove them for the sins that they have committed;
And Your goodness is upon those who sin, when they repent.
9.17:
For You chose the seed of Aḇraham before all the nations,
And set Your name upon us, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
9.18:
And You will not reject us forever.
You made a covenant with our fathers concerning us;
9.19:
And we hope in You, when our being turns to You.
The mercy of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be upon the house of Yisra’ĕl forever and ever.
